chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, the Exalted:
“Bring a Qur’an other than this, or change it.”
He عليه السلام said: “They said: Or change ʿAlī عليه السلام.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.عَلِيًّا: ʿAlī عليه السلام, whose mention is indicated in the commentary
key_terms.قَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: the statement of Allah, the Exalted

ai.seo_question: How is the verse “Bring a Qur’an other than this or change it” interpreted in relation to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a quranic commentary in which the demand to alter the revelation is understood as a demand to alter what it indicates regarding ʿAlī عليه السلام. It connects the verse to the question of wilayah and the rejection of divinely appointed authority.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Al Husayn Bin Umar Bin Yazeed, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted
[10:15] Bring a Quran other than this or change it. Say: It does not beseem me that I should change it from myself
en.sarwar: 37. Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ’Isma‘il ibn Mihran from al-Hassan al-Qummi from Idris ibn ‘Abdallah who has said the following.
“I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the interpretation of this verse of the Holy Quran.
“They will reply, “We did not pray,” [74:43].

The Imam (a.s.)said, “Such people will be those who did believe in the Imams about whom Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has saaid, “ (The foremost ones) will be the nearest ones to God” [56:11] Have not noticed that people call the one second to the lead in horse racing ‘al-Musalli’ (the praying)? This is what is meant therein. “We did not pray’ means ‘we did not follow the lead’.”
